transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-11 15:00 PT
Duration: 1h15m
Attendees: Jordan Mills (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (Redwood Sales Ops), Aisha Rahman (Peregrine - Head of ML), Tom Becker (Platform Eng), Ravi Patel (Product), Maya Soto (Security)

Auto-summary (auto): quick sparring, lots of live roleplay, some noisy audio on Maya at times

---
00:00:03 Jordan (AE): okay, hi everyone thanks for joining, this is our champion sparring, the idea is we grill the answers, practice the messaging, and then Priya will run a 5 minute demo snippet where we intentionally trigger fallback scenarios.
00:00:17 Aisha: hey Jordan thanks, excited, we wanted to see how you'd answer the usual POC questions, esp around latency and our on-prem constraints.
00:00:25 Priya (SE): great, we'll do rapid-fire objections. Quick note, we'll call out Dedicated = reserved GPU pools, Private = VPC/on-prem, sometimes in the field folks say "Redwood Dedicate" or "Redwood private plane" — ignore typos.
00:00:42 Tom: haha yeah names get scrambled a lot. can you give the one-liner vs OpenAI?
00:00:48 Jordan: sure. Redwood's short pitch: we provide a production-first inference platform that lets you pick hosted for speed, Dedicated for throughput predictability, or Private for compliance, while keeping the same API and rollout tooling. Contrast that with a pure model provider where you get a model but not the operational pieces — latency SLOs, batching, autoscaling, that kind of stuff.
00:01:10 Ravi: so why not just use OpenAI and set up their gateway?
00:01:14 Jordan: good, so we roleplay that: the quick rebuttal is — OpenAI gives managed model access but you're giving up control over deployment behaviors and often cost predictability at scale. With Redwood you get explicit knobs: batching, KV caching/ prefix cache, and quantization profiles to lower unit cost; we provide predictable dedicated pools and SLAs.
00:01:36 Aisha: hmm kv cache? can you explain that one more time, I still hear KV cash in our notes sometimes.
00:01:42 Priya: yes — KV cache, it's the key-value KV cache used for transformer context reuse, it avoids regen of prefix tokens. In practice we call out prefix caching and per-customer cache hits; that reduces both latency for interactive flows and token cost.
00:01:58 Maya: and what's the encryption story, do you support our KMS?
00:02:02 Jordan: yes, we integrate with cloud KMS and HSM options for Private deployments; for Hosted we offer customer-managed keys as an add-on, and we can walk through the architecture doc. Liam will post the SOC 2 summary and a KMS integration note after this call.
00:02:20 Liam: noted, will attach links: link to deck: https://redwood.app/comp-playbook.pdf and SOC2 summary: https://redwood.app/soc2-summary.pdf
00:02:28 Tom: great thanks. now let's do the competitive script practice — Priya you play the customer who cares about latency but also cost. Jordan you have 2 minutes to pitch and close.
00:02:40 Priya (as customer): okay I'm focused on 99th percentile latency under 200ms for routing, but we have a hard cost target per million tokens. show me why Redwood.
00:02:51 Jordan: short answer: two levers. First, smart routing — route requests by latency or cost tier, you can fall back to cheaper quantized variants during peak load. Second, batching + prefix/KV caching reduces per-token work which lowers unit cost. Also Dedicated pools give you predictable throughput so P99s stabilize. Example: in our recent telco pilot we shaved 30% off per-token cost with KV cache and a ~20ms P99 improvement using tuned kernels.
00:03:27 Priya (customer): okay can you quantify the tradeoffs?
00:03:30 Jordan: yes, we usually run a quick benchmark: pick your model family and sequence length; we'll run a 50k token/day sim under your QPS distribution. We compare Hosted with Dedicated and a Private on your infra. We'll give a numbers table: cost per 1M tokens, median latency, P99 latency.
00:03:51 Aisha: how do you handle rollouts? if we ship a model and then find regressions?
00:03:55 Priya: rollout tools include canary, A/B, automatic fallback to a stable variant. We tie regressions to evals and prompt sets so you can stop a rollout if quality drops.
00:04:06 Ravi: what's the model catalog like — can we bring custom models?
00:04:09 Jordan: absolutely; we onboard open models and customer models. We also provide quantization recommendations. For custom models on Private, you control the infra and we provide the runtime.
00:04:21 Tom: demo time?
00:04:23 Priya: yes — I'll share screen (note: audio hiccup).
00:04:30 [00:04:30] Priya (SE): starting demo — showing latency dashboard, token breakdown by route, then I'll trigger fallback by throttling Dedicated pool to emulate a surge.
00:04:45 [00:05:10] Priya: (narration) here is trace for a request: token breakdown shows prefix cache 42% hit, batching saved 18% tokens, and routing moved to a compat quantized model when thresholds hit. the UI shows transparent fallback and automatic retry logic.
00:05:40 Jordan: small note — sometimes the transcript generator writes "prefix cash" or "K V cash" — not K-V cache, but you get it.
00:05:52 [00:06:20] Ravi: in that fallback case are we losing quality? how do we measure that?
00:06:24 Priya: we attach quality monitors and regression alerts tied to prompt evaluation sets; you can configure thresholds for automatic rollback. Also we track hallucination metrics and perplexity proxies.
00:06:40 Speaker 1 (customer): are you supporting SSO + RBAC for devs? we want tight controls.
00:06:45 Jordan: yes, SAML/SSO and role-based access control are available, plus audit logs per token and per-route. For Private we can integrate with your identity provider.
00:06:58 [00:07:10] Aisha: okay, now some hostile questions — Ravi will pose as our procurement who only cares about cost and vendor lock-in. Jordan you have 90 seconds.
00:07:20 Ravi (procurement): Why not build this in house? we already have a team that can stitch models + Kubernetes.
00:07:26 Jordan: fair — in-house gives control but has hidden ops cost: optimizing kernels, managing KV cache, continuous kernel selection for different sequence distributions, and having observability tied to per-token economics. Redwood packages that expertise and reduces time-to-produce by months, plus we provide SLOs and SLAs you won't get out of an internal PoC.
00:07:49 Priya: in addition, our runtime has production tokenizer and attention optimizations that are non-trivial to reimplement and maintain.
00:07:58 Tom: ok good. now let's do lightning rebuttals to the following quick prompts: "data residency", "quantization quality loss", "vendor lock-in" — Jordan you call out the 20 second answer and then longer follow-up if needed.
00:08:12 Jordan: data residency — short: Private deployment and regional hosting options, audit logs and KMS; long: we offer air-gapped packages for regulated verticals and per-tenant data separation. Quantization quality loss — short: small delta for many families, we recommend quant profiles per workload and run evals pre-rollout; long: we keep golden baseline evals and show A/B quality comparisons. Vendor lock-in — short: same API across modes and easy export of models and data, long: we support model snapshots and exportable config, plus migration playbooks.
00:08:48 Maya: quick question on air-gapped — does Redwood run agents in our network or do you ship a binary?
00:08:54 Priya: both options; for full air-gap we ship an on-prem package, for Private VPC it's a customer-controlled control plane and our runtime as images you deploy.
00:09:05 [00:09:25] Jordan: (roleplay note) okay now we flip roles — Aisha will give us her toughest buyer persona, we want crisp one-liners and follow-ups.
00:09:35 Aisha (as buyer): I care about predictable latency under heavy load, but I also need to reduce cost 40% vs current vendor contract.
00:09:42 Jordan: one-liner: Redwood lowers unit cost with caching + batching and gives predictable throughput with Dedicated — we can run a pilot with measurable metric targets and a money-back style clause for the bench.
00:09:56 Aisha: hmm money-back?
00:09:58 Jordan: (laugh) not legal-approved here, but we can scope a pilot with success criteria and credits if we miss targets.
00:10:05 [00:10:30] Ravi: switching gears, let's surface some microscripts: A) "What if we need private keys in HSM?" B) "How do you handle PCI or PHI?"
00:10:40 Priya: A) HSM + KMS integration available for Private; Hosted can support customer-managed keys with additional controls. B) For PHI/PCI, use Private on-prem or VPC, and we offer compliance packages and logging for audit; we'll loop in security for the technical attestation.
00:10:58 Maya: we'll need concrete architecture diagrams.
00:11:01 Liam: I'll attach the architecture diagram and the enclave notes after the call.
00:11:10 [00:11:40] Jordan: quick objection training: customer says "OpenAI is cheaper and faster" — answer: OpenAI can be faster to start but at scale per-token costs and lack of custom routing/rollout features cause unpredictable bills; we provide quantified benchmarking and a migration plan plus Dedicated which flattens tail latency.
00:12:05 Priya: roleplay — I'm the technical buyer pushing on kernels: "How do you pick kernels for different sequence lengths?"
00:12:11 Jordan: runtime inspects model arch and sequence distribution and selects optimized kernels; we also keep a library of platform-optimized kernels per GPU type. Sometimes the transcript writes "kernel selection" as "kernel affection"— ignore that.
00:12:30 [00:12:55] Aisha: this was super helpful. now for the final practice — Jordan will do a live cold close with all of us as stakeholders.
00:13:05 Jordan: quick recap: Redwood gives you a single API, predictable options (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), operational primitives (KV cache, batching, routing), and observability to tie quality to cost. Next step: we'll run a scoped pilot with goals: P99 under 200ms on typical flows, 30% unit cost reduction target, and SOC2/KMS integration validated. Who owns what?
00:13:32 Aisha: I'll be internal champion, will coordinate with procurement and security.
00:13:36 Maya: send the SOC 2 and KMS integration notes.
00:13:40 Jordan: will do. Liam will attach pricing scenarios too.
00:13:45 Liam: yes, will update CRM with pricing tiers and two pilot options: 8-week Dedicated pilot, or 12-week Private validation.
00:13:53 [00:14:05] Jordan: quick feedback for enablement team — during roleplays, avoid saying "we're just an API" as that plays into the "no ops" angle; prefer "we're the inference runtime + ops layer". Also prep one short video clip showing fallback in 30s.
00:14:25 Aisha: we liked the kernel talk, could you give that to our platform folks in a separate tech deep dive?
00:14:30 Priya: yes, schedule SE deep dive — Priya will run kernel + on-prem deployment deep dive.
00:14:38 Jordan: recap of next steps (read verbatim): 1) Jordan to share rebuttal playbook and updated deck link; 2) Priya to record 3 demo clips (fallbacks, caching, rollout) and a kernel deep-dive deck; 3) Liam to attach pricing scenarios and SOC 2 summary to CRM; 4) schedule follow-up roleplay with Aisha and a technical deep dive with Tom.
00:15:05 Ravi: sounds good.
00:15:12 Maya: small audio glitch earlier, but overall fine.
00:15:20 Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up by EOD with the materials and propose times for next week.
01:14:50 [01:14:50] (call end)
